title: The drift guard resolves `actual = readPhaseModel(phase, repoConfigPath)` witho…
description:
The drift guard resolves `actual = readPhaseModel(phase, repoConfigPath)` without threading the resolved backend, then for a non-claude phase asserts isClaudeAliasModel(actual) is false. Since the committed config is all-claude this is correct today, but if a future codex phase set only a nested [models.codex] key (no flat fallback), the un-threaded read would return the claude DEFAULT (opus) and the guard would falsely redden. Consider threading `backend` into the readPhaseModel call so the drift guard validates the spawn-accurate model. Non-blocking; matches the AC as written.

Source: cam/issue-356
Review round: 1

suggestion-fingerprint: 66d2e2a5927d

spec.scope: Thread the resolved backend into the drift-guard test so it validates the spawn-accurate model instead of the flat/DEFAULT fallback. In test/config/models.test.ts, the drift-guard describe block ('readPhaseModel vs repo project.toml (drift guard)', ~lines 750-773) currently calls readPhaseModel(phase, repoConfigPath) with no backend argument, then resolves readPhaseBackend one line later. Resolve readPhaseBackend(phase, repoConfigPath) BEFORE the readPhaseModel call and pass it as the third positional argument: readPhaseModel(phase, repoConfigPath, backend). Also make the `expected` value that is compared against `actual` use the same backend-aware resolution order that readPhaseModel uses (nested [models.<backend>].<phase>, then flat [models].<phase>, then DEFAULTS[phase]) so the equality assertion holds for both claude and a future codex phase. Confined to the test file; no production source change (readPhaseModel already accepts the backend param).
acceptanceCriteria: The drift-guard test resolves readPhaseBackend(phase, repoConfigPath) and passes that backend as the third argument to readPhaseModel(phase, repoConfigPath, backend).

The `expected` value compared against `actual` in the equality assertion is derived with the same backend-aware resolution order as readPhaseModel (nested [models.<backend>].<phase>, then flat [models].<phase>, then DEFAULTS[phase]), so the equality assertion holds for both a claude phase and a hypothetical [models.<backend>]-only codex phase.
bun test test/config/models.test.ts passes: every per-phase drift-guard case is green against the committed all-claude scripts/cam/project.toml.
No production source file is modified; the change is confined to test/config/models.test.ts (readPhaseModel already accepts the optional backend param).
bun run typecheck passes and the full bun test suite stays green.
gotchas: readPhaseModel already has signature (phase, configPath?, backend?); do NOT add a new parameter or change any source file. Other call sites (plan-runner.ts, loop.ts, review.ts, run.ts, config.ts) already thread backend the same way.

readNestedBackendModel returns undefined when backend is omitted OR equals 'claude', falling through to the flat lookup. For the committed all-claude config, threading backend is a no-op and the suite stays green today.

Threading backend into `actual` WITHOUT also making `expected` backend-aware would merely relocate the latent false-redden from the isClaudeAliasModel assertion (line 769) to the equality assertion (lines 762-763) in a future [models.<backend>]-only config. Update both.
The drift guard reads the REAL repo config (scripts/cam/project.toml via process.cwd()), not a tmp fixture. Keep it reading the real config; do not introduce a tmp fixture.
